results.title: Ghana Publishing Company introduces online system to combat fake gazettes
results.content: The Ghana Publishing Company Limited (GPCL) has introduced an online verification system to help individuals and institutions confirm the authenticity of gazettes and curb the circulation of fake documents. The system allows the public to check whether a gazette is genuine without having to visit the company's offices. Speaking at a press conference in Accra on Monday, October 19, 2026, GPCL Managing Director, Nana Kwasi Boatey, Esq., said the initiative forms part of efforts to address the problem of fake gazettes. He said the company had already taken steps to tackle the issue, but the new online system would make it easier for the public to distinguish genuine publications from fraudulent ones.

results.title: Ghana’s flood response needs engineers trained in sustainable drainage – USTED project lead
results.content: Ghana’s response to urban flooding may depend partly on what future engineers learn in the classroom, with a university-led project calling for sustainable drainage systems to become part of construction education. Pro Vice-Chancellor of the University of Skills Training and Entrepreneurial Development (USTED), and project lead, Professor Isaac Boateng, says engineers must be trained to do more than construct drains as the country confronts the pressures of urban expansion, intense rainfall and inadequate stormwater management. “The question is no longer simply whether we can construct drains. It is whether we can design, build and maintain drainage systems that protect people, conserve resources and support sustainable urban development,” he said. His comments come as USTED and Edinburgh Napier University in Scotland work to integrate Sustainable Urban Drainage Systems (SuDS) into Ghana

results.title: University Basic School, Legon, wins CSIR quiz for third consecutive year
results.content: The University Basic School (UBS), Legon, has won the 2026 Council for Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR)-Food Research Institute Quiz Competition, securing its third consecutive title with 70 points. UBS finished ahead of Christ the King International School, which scored 63 points, The Ridge Church School with 50 points, and Armed Forces Basic School with 47 points. The competition was held at the CSIR-Food Research Institute's conference hall at Shiashie in Accra as part of activities to commemorate World Food Day, observed annually on October 16. The latest victory extends UBS's winning streak since it first participated in the competition in 2024, having also emerged champion in the 2024 and 2025 editions.

The discussions followed an engagement with Microsoft employees under the company's Africa Giving Campaign, which provided a platform for the climate-focused organisations to explore how Microsoft's technical expertise, digital tools and employee volunteerism could support their work. results.title: Global South urged to unite despite differences – Prof Opoku-Agyemang
results.content: Vice-President Professor Jane Naana Opoku-Agyemang has urged countries in the Global South to strengthen cooperation despite differences in their political systems, histories and development experiences. Speaking at the 2026 Global South Academic Forum in Shanghai, China, she said countries must learn to disagree respectfully while pursuing common development goals, particularly amid growing global polarisation. Professor Opoku-Agyemang stressed that unity should not require countries to hold identical positions on every issue. “A unified voice should not be a uniform voice,” she said.

results.title: Vice President urges political parties to prioritise policy research and institutional knowledge
results.content: Vice-President Professor Jane Naana Opoku-Agyemang has urged political parties to prioritise policy research and institutional knowledge to strengthen governance and sustain effective administration beyond changes in leadership.
